---
title: "R(eal) Basics"
author: "Franz X. Mohr"
date: "2019-10-06"
description: "A series of introductions on essential R skills for beginners. These range from the basic user interface of R and RStudio to data manipulation with the dplyr, data.table and sparklyr packages and visualisation with the ggplot2 package."
---

This section should help you to

* [get R and RStudio started on your computer](/rbasics/installation)
* [understand the structure of the program](/rbasics/rstructure)
* [prepare your workspace for an analysis](/rbasics/beforestart)
* [import data, get help and some more important vocabulary](/rbasics/help_and_data_import_etc)
* [manipulate data with the `dplyr` package](/rbasics/dplyrintro)
* [manipulate data with the `data.table` package](/rbasics/datatableintro)
* [manipulate data which does not fit into memory with the `sparklyr` package](/rbasics/sparklyrintro)
* [create graphics with the `ggplot2` package](/rbasics/ggplotintro).

Recently, I have finished the first version of a below 30 pages introduction to R. It uses an exemplary workflow to explain some basics of the language and the application of the packages `dplyr`, `ggplot2` and `openxlsx`. The script can be downloaded <a href="/2019-mohr-introduction-r.pdf" target="_blank">here</a>.
